steps.announcement: Start with a sorted prefix containing only 4.
steps.explanation: Initially, the first element, 4 at index 0, forms the sorted prefix [0, 0] on its own. The next pass will insert the 1 at index 1 into this prefix.
steps.key_state: Initially nums = [4, 1, 3, 1, 5, 2], with sorted prefix [0, 0]. The next value to insert is 1 at index 1.
steps.title: Start with a one-element prefix

steps.announcement: Pass 1 is complete. The 1 has been inserted before 4.
steps.explanation: Pass 1 takes the 1 at index 1, shifts the larger 4 in the prefix right to index 1, and writes 1 to index 0. The sorted prefix grows to [0, 1]. Next comes the 3 at index 2.
steps.key_state: After pass 1, nums = [1, 4, 3, 1, 5, 2], with sorted prefix [0, 1]. Next comes the 3 at index 2.
steps.title: Insert 1 before 4

steps.announcement: Pass 2 is complete. The 3 has been inserted between 1 and 4.
steps.explanation: Pass 2 takes the 3 at index 2. Only 4 in the prefix exceeds 3, so shift 4 right to index 2 and insert 3 at index 1, between 1 and 4. The sorted prefix grows to [0, 2]. Next comes the 1 at index 3.
steps.key_state: After pass 2, nums = [1, 3, 4, 1, 5, 2], with sorted prefix [0, 2]. Next comes the 1 at index 3.
steps.title: Insert 3 between 1 and 4

steps.announcement: Pass 3 is complete. The second 1 has been inserted after the first, preserving their order.
steps.explanation: Pass 3 takes the second 1, at index 3, and shifts the larger values 4 and 3 right in turn. Shifting stops as soon as the scan reaches the equal first 1 at index 0. Insert the second 1 just after it at index 1, preserving their original order. Next comes the 5 at index 4. The sorted prefix is now [0, 3].
steps.key_state: After pass 3, nums = [1, 1, 3, 4, 5, 2], with sorted prefix [0, 3]. Next comes the 5 at index 4. The two 1s retain their original order.
steps.title: Insert the second 1 after the first

steps.announcement: Pass 4 is complete. The 5 stayed in place, and the sorted prefix grew.
steps.explanation: Pass 4 takes the 5 at index 4. It exceeds 4, the largest value in the sorted prefix [1, 1, 3, 4], so nothing shifts right. The 5 joins the prefix in place, extending it to [0, 4]. Next comes the 2 at index 5.
steps.key_state: After pass 4, nums = [1, 1, 3, 4, 5, 2], with sorted prefix [0, 4]. Next comes the 2 at index 5. No elements moved as 5 joined the prefix.
steps.title: Add 5 to the sorted prefix

steps.announcement: Pass 5 is complete. The 2 has been inserted after the two 1s, completing the sort.
steps.explanation: Pass 5 takes the final 2 at index 5 and shifts the larger values 5, 4, and 3 one place right in turn. Insert 2 after the two 1s at index 2. The sorted prefix now covers [0, 5], completing the sort.
steps.key_state: After pass 5, nums = [1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5], with sorted prefix [0, 5]. Sorting is complete.
steps.title: Insert 2 after both 1s

prose.summary: The six states show the initial array and the array after passes 1 through 5. The animation step number is one greater than the number of completed passes.
prose.title: Insertion sort pass by pass

context: Initially nums = [4, 1, 3, 1, 5, 2], with indices 0 through 5. The single-element range holding the first element, 4, is already sorted. The initial sorted range is therefore [0, 0].
Each pass takes the element immediately to the right of the sorted prefix as base, shifts larger elements right, and writes base into the position that opens up.
description: Only the order within the prefix is guaranteed. Its elements may still shift right when smaller elements are inserted later.
Pass 3 inserts the second 1. Shifting stops at the equal first 1, preserving their original order. The 5 in pass 4 needs no move, but the prefix still grows. Pass 5 inserts 2 to finish sorting.

frames.explanation: After five passes, the sorted prefix covers the whole array and the two 1s remain in their original order.
frames.title: Insertion sort pass by pass

summary: Each pass inserts the next element on the right into the sorted prefix, extending it by one.
